messages:
jonah_sales: Heads-up — Acme wants a temporary quota increase while they finish onboarding. They want 2x committed tokens for 14 days. Sales asking if we can do this without changing the contract yet.
ashley_product: Is this a hard commit change or a one-off trial? Important for pricing/forecast.
jonah_sales: One-off. They won't sign until they see the perf with their traffic shape.
mike_ops: Operationally doable as a scoped override on their quota + routing priority but we need to think about capacity and billing. If we allow 2x burst, other tenants might be impacted during peak.
ashley_product: Proposal: offer a "trial burst" add-on that is time-boxed and metered. Two pieces: 1) a temporary soft-cap lift (no SLA change), 2) a billed usage multiplier for extra tokens.
elaine_legal: Need a short addendum that limits liability and clarifies no SLA expansion. Also track start/end dates and automatic reversion. I can draft a one-paragraph clause.
jonah_sales: That sounds fine. Customer expects simple email confirmation, not a full contract amend.
mike_ops: Implementation details:
```
# pseudo-config
customer_overrides:
  acme: {
    burst_multiplier: 2.0,
    start: "2024-06-01",
    end: "2024-06-15",
    billing_mode: "metered",
  }
```
We'll need an ops job to reconcile usage and tag overage tokens for billing.
ashley_product: Launch criteria for this add-on to ship as a self-serve or manual? I prefer manual first (SE-assisted) because of capacity risk and edge cases. 
jonah_sales: SE-assisted is OK for now — we just need a playbook and pricing table.
mike_ops: Playbook items:
- capacity check (do we have spare slots in region X?)
- routing policy: deprioritize burst traffic under severe contention
- billing tag applied for extra tokens
- telemetry alert if usage > 3x expected during trial
elaine_legal: Simple addendum text I propose: "Temporary trial burst provided for evaluation only. Redwood Inference's standard SLA and limits remain in effect; no warranty of uninterrupted service. Trial expires automatically; customer liable for billed overages."
ashley_product: Pricing options to present to customer (short list):
- Flat trial fee + metered overage at standard rate
- Meter-only: bill only for additional tokens at 1.8x unit price
- Deferred reconciliation: credit account if they convert to commit within 30 days (requires finance sign-off)
Which is preferred for a low-friction sale?
jonah_sales: Meter-only preferred by the customer. They want to see real cost numbers before committing.
mike_ops: Finance/ops note: need to ensure invoicing can tag these tokens differently. Graceful fallback: if billing pipeline can't separate trial tokens, we'll do manual invoice line items.
ashley_product: Next steps: Elaine to draft clause, Mike to draft ops playbook + telemetry hooks, Jonah to confirm customer prefers meter-only and dates. I'll collect pricing and add to the SE playbook.
elaine_legal: Drafted clause. Posting here for quick review: "Temporary Burst Addendum: Customer granted a one-time, time-limited increase to service quota (\"Burst\"), subject to start and end dates. Burst is provided for evaluation. No change to warranties or SLA levels. Charges incurred by Burst usage are billable and due under standard payment terms. Redwood reserves right to throttle or suspend Burst in case of infrastructure risk." :thumbsup:
mike_ops: I'll stub the playbook doc in Confluence + create a small runbook snippet for on-call. Also will add a deploy-bot check to prevent overlapping bursts in same pool.
deploy-bot: automated-note: added 'burst-overlap-guard' flag to infra deployment pipeline (PR #4872).
jonah_sales: I'll confirm dates with Acme tomorrow and ping here. Thanks all.
ashley_product: Good. We'll treat this as a low-risk add-on pilot. If it becomes common, we should productize a self-serve 'trial burst' with UI and billing automation.
jonah_sales: +1. End of thread.
